attribution.note: Both occurrences are Marcus's own words on his Substack. In o1 he rejects Musk's prediction. In o2 he states his own bet that superhuman AGI would not arrive by end of 2025. Musk's words are quoted only as the target.

semantics.note: A $1M bet that AGI superior to the smartest humans would not arrive by end 2025 is an unhedged commitment, so this is a scored forecast. The normalisation keeps Marcus's own reading (any intellectual work any human can do) and the 2025-12-31 horizon.

contract.note: Marcus supplied the test himself: one piece of intellectual work the best humans can do that AGI can't. Treating a human-validated task set that no verified AI fully solved as such work applies his test directly. A reasonable alternative reading would not flip the result.

evidence.note: Dated 2025-12-05, before the deadline. ARC Prize reports the best verified systems at 37.6% and 54% on ARC-AGI-2, so no verified system solved the set in full.
May 2025 preprint. Every ARC-AGI-2 task was solved by at least two people in two attempts or less. Combined with the December AI scores, this shows tasks that humans did and AI did not.

output.rationale: The deadline 2025-12-31 has passed. Pre-deadline measurements show every ARC-AGI-2 task was solved by humans, while the best verified AI reached only 54%. That leaves intellectual work humans can do and AI could not, which meets Marcus's own test and the support condition. Nothing in the packet shows an AI able to do any human intellectual work by end 2025. Scores cover only verified systems, but the contradiction condition is plainly unmet.
